chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
The sacrificial animal (hady) of the Hajj is from the Hajj (expenditure).

key_terms.هَدِيَّةُ: Sacrificial animal offered during Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: Is the cost of the sacrificial animal considered part of the Hajj expenditure?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the phrase 'hady of Hajj is from Hajj' establishes that the sacrificial animal is an intrinsic component of the pilgrimage ritual rather than a separate financial obligation. This ruling clarifies that the expenditure for the hady is legally subsumed under the general requirements of Hajj, influencing how scholars calculate the validity and completeness of the pilgrimage rites. It underscores the holistic nature of Hajj obligations in Shia jurisprudence, where the sacrificial act is viewed as an extension of the pilgrimage itself.
